result:
The proposed answer of 3 is very likely wrong, and its justification does not hold up.

The cited source, "IMC 2011 Problem 10", has nothing to do with tree decompositions with bounded spread, so the argument is unsupported.

My recollection of the literature, which I cannot check here, is that every graph has a tree decomposition of width at most about 2·tw(G)+1 in which each vertex's spread is O(d(v)+1). If that holds, then P(c) is true for every c a bit above 2. For example, P(2.5) holds, because 2·tw+1 ≤ 2.5·tw once tw ≥ 2, and forests (tw ≤ 1) can be handled directly. That would force α to be at most about 2, so α = 3 cannot be right. The true threshold in that line of work is, I believe, smaller (something like 4/3), though I have not confirmed the exact value.

VERDICT: REJECT
